*.battery.mfr-date: A manufacturing date — the name states both the subject and the kind of value, and NUT reports nothing else
*.commands.driver-private-cmd: A driver-private instant command: the button sends exactly this name to the driver, and the adapter cannot know what the driver does with it
*.commands.driver-private-unknown: A driver-private instant command outside the NUT catalog: the name is the literal command sent, and an invented sentence would describe some other driver
*.device.contact: The name resolves the only ambiguity there is — this is the administrator's name, not a dry contact
*.device.description: Free text an administrator stored on the device; the adapter can say nothing the name does not
*.device.location: Free text an administrator stored on the device — where it stands; the name is the whole content
*.device.mfr: Plain hardware identification: NUT reports the manufacturer and nothing more, so the label is the whole content
*.device.model: Plain hardware identification: the model designation the device reports, and nothing beyond it
*.device.serial: Plain hardware identification: an opaque serial number — a sentence could only repeat the name
*.driver.flag-weird: A driver-private flag: the name is the driver's own, and the adapter cannot know what a private flag means
*.driver.name: The NUT driver's program name, e.g. usbhid-ups — a sentence could only repeat it
*.driver.version-usb: The name already says which of the driver's versions this is: the USB library it was built against
*.ups.firmware: The UPS firmware version as an opaque string — name and value are the whole statement
*.ups.firmware-aux: NUT specifies nothing beyond 'auxiliary device firmware'; the name is as specific as the protocol gets
*.ups.mfr: Legacy twin of the device manufacturer that NUT will drop — plain identification, the label is the whole content
*.ups.mfr-date: A manufacturing date — the name states both the subject and the kind of value, and NUT reports nothing else
*.ups.model: Legacy twin of the device model that NUT will drop — plain identification, nothing beyond the designation
*.ups.serial: Legacy twin of the device serial number that NUT will drop — an opaque string the name fully describes
